knowledge_point: Gravity produces downward acceleration when other forces are small.
Projectile motion combines nearly constant horizontal velocity with vertical gravitational acceleration.
Friction dissipates mechanical energy and reduces sliding speed.
Momentum transfer in contact collisions redistributes velocity and direction.
Inelastic collisions dissipate kinetic energy through deformation, heat, sound, or sticking.
A pendulum exchanges gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy over each swing.
Damping dissipates oscillator energy, causing amplitude decay over time.
Resonance amplifies motion when periodic forcing matches a natural frequency.
Bernoulli/Venturi flow couples higher speed through a constriction with lower static pressure.
Buoyancy depends on displaced fluid weight relative to object weight.
Pressure gradients drive siphon or liquid-column flow after priming.
Surface tension minimizes liquid surface area, driving droplets to retract and round.
Capillary action draws wetting liquids through narrow pores or tubes.
Wetting transitions occur when adhesion overcomes nonwetting surface forces.
Differential thermal expansion bends bonded materials when heated.
The Leidenfrost effect forms a vapor layer that delays contact boiling and lets droplets glide.
Magnetic dipoles experience torque that aligns them with an external magnetic field.
Electric fields exert forces on charged droplets or particles, driving migration or deformation.
Supersaturation enables nucleation followed by crystal growth.
Solidification fronts propagate as liquid changes phase into ordered solid.
Iodine-clock kinetics delay starch-iodine color until reductant is depleted.
Reducing sugars reduce copper(II) to copper(I) oxide during Benedict heating.
Redox indicator systems can cycle between colored oxidation states.
Ion mixing can exceed solubility product and produce an insoluble solid.
Local supersaturation at a reaction interface creates precipitate bands or membranes.
Gas-evolution reactions generate bubbles as products leave solution.
Combustion requires fuel, oxidizer, and heat; removing one extinguishes flame.
Concentration gradients drive molecular diffusion and spreading.
Laminar shear stretches and folds fluids, increasing interface without turbulence.
Shear-thickening suspensions resist rapid stress while flowing under slow stress.
Heating can soften or melt material, reducing strength and enabling deformation.
Mitotic spindle dynamics separate chromosomes into daughter cells.
Cytokinesis completes division through progressive contractile-ring constriction.
Actin polymerization and adhesion cycles drive crawling cell migration.
Osmosis changes plant-cell volume, causing plasmolysis and deplasmolysis.
Guard-cell turgor changes open and close stomatal pores.
Cytoplasmic streaming moves organelles along cytoskeletal tracks inside plant cells.
Photosynthetic light reactions release oxygen when illuminated.
Cellular respiration consumes oxygen and releases carbon dioxide during metabolism.
Embryogenesis proceeds through repeated cell divisions and coordinated cell migration.
Seed germination starts with water uptake and radicle emergence before shoot development.
Phototropism bends shoots through differential growth toward directional light.
Gravitropism redirects root or shoot growth relative to gravity after reorientation.
Hydrotropism biases root growth toward water gradients.
Thigmonasty converts touch stimulation into rapid leaf or trap movement.
Nyctinasty changes leaf posture across light-dark cycles via turgor or growth rhythms.
Jet propulsion follows momentum conservation: expelled fluid creates opposite reaction thrust.
Peristaltic locomotion uses contraction waves plus alternating anchors to move soft bodies.
Flapping wings generate lift and thrust by accelerating air downward/backward.
Fast-start swimming converts body curvature into hydrodynamic reaction forces and acceleration.
Chemotaxis biases movement direction along chemical concentration gradients.
Phototaxis biases movement relative to light direction or intensity.
Magnetotaxis aligns motile cells with a magnetic field through magnetic torque.
Run-and-tumble or Levy-like search alternates runs and turns to explore space.
Moist convection lifts air, cools it, and forms growing cloud towers.
Rotating atmospheric flow organizes clouds and precipitation into vortices.
Gravity and hydraulic slope drive surface runoff and channelized flow.
Infiltration advances a wetting front through porous soil.
Sediment motion begins when fluid shear stress exceeds a transport threshold.
Deposition and sorting occur because particle settling speed depends on size and density.
Slope failure occurs when driving stress exceeds material shear strength.
Pyroclastic density currents move as ground-hugging particle-laden gravity currents.
Lava flow forms a cooling crust while molten interior continues advancing.
Glacier flow results from ice deformation and basal sliding.
Glacier calving occurs when fractures propagate and unsupported ice detaches.
Predation is a dynamic interaction of pursuit, attack, and prey response.
Animal-mediated pollination transfers pollen through contact with reproductive structures.
Linkage constraints convert input rotation into a designed output path.
Cam profiles convert continuous rotation into programmed follower displacement.
Escapements discretize energy release into stepwise gear advance.
Ratchets allow intermittent one-way motion while blocking reverse motion.
Valves regulate flow by changing flow area and pressure drop.
Pumps use cyclic volume or pressure changes to impose one-way fluid transport.
Feedback control reduces deviation by sensing a variable and actuating a correction.
Pressure-driven filtration separates solids by forcing fluid through porous media.
Density-driven settling separates particles by gravitational settling velocity.
Vibration can segregate granular mixtures when smaller grains percolate downward.
Mechanical mixing disperses components by stretching, folding, and advecting interfaces.
Coating/wetting processes rely on contact-angle reduction and droplet coalescence into a film.
Hot forging uses elevated temperature to lower flow stress for controlled plastic deformation.
Quenching rapidly extracts heat to change material state and properties.
Cutting forms chips when tool shear stress exceeds material strength along a shear plane.
Drilling combines rotary cutting and axial feed to remove material as chips.
Mechanical resonance can amplify vibration until structural instability or failure occurs.
Clogging creates positive feedback by reducing flow area and increasing upstream accumulation.
